report.source_text: Based on the NGS results (Oncomine Comprehensive Assay, Thermo Fisher Scientific), the tumour had two major somatic mutations, BRAF V600E and TP53 H179Q mutation. TP53 H179 is known as a missense mutation that worsens prognosis.1 The mutation allele frequency (MAF) of BRAF was 0.483 and that of TP53 was 0.916. The MAF values showed that this mutation in TP53 caused mutations in both alleles of DNA. On the other hand, BRAF V600E mutation is known to cause deletion of one allele, loss of heterozygosity, and the BRAF MAF value close to 0.5 indicated that most of the cells had the BRAF V600E mutation.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Mixed adenocarcinoma and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) of lung origin with cerebellar metastasis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 57-year-old woman with a smoking history presented with progressive headache, vomiting, and balance loss. Brain MRI identified a 45 mm cystic mass in the right cerebellum. Biopsy of the cerebellar lesion showed a mixture of adenocarcinoma and LCNEC components with positive TTF-1 staining, suggesting lung origin. Whole-body CT revealed a right pulmonary hilum tumor and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Mediastinal lymph node biopsy found LCNEC cells without adenocarcinoma. Molecular analysis detected BRAF V600E and TP53 H179Q mutations, with immunostaining confirming BRAF V600E mutation in both tumor components. These findings confirmed the diagnosis of mixed adenocarcinoma and LCNEC metastasizing to the cerebellum from a primary lung cancer.
